tour.overview:
Washington, D.C., was planned in the 1790s as the capital of the new United States, with grand avenues and the National Mall, a two-mile green stretching from the Capitol to the Lincoln Memorial. Along it stand the country's great monuments and memorials and the museums of the Smithsonian Institution, most of them free.

This private day shows the capital with a local guide and a vehicle, linking the monuments, the seat of government, a museum and Arlington National Cemetery across the Potomac.

AT A GLANCE
• Duration: about 8 hours
• Start and end: your hotel in Washington, D.C.
• Type: private tour with local guide, vehicle and driver
• Booking: on request – we confirm availability and the final price by email within 24 hours, and you pay only then
• Level: easy to moderate; walks on the Mall

WHAT YOU SEE
• The Lincoln Memorial and the war memorials.
• The Washington Monument and the Jefferson Memorial.
• The White House.
• The Capitol and the Library of Congress.
• A Smithsonian museum.
• Arlington National Cemetery.

WHY THIS WORKS
The monuments are spread over several kilometres; the vehicle lets you see them all and still have time for a museum.

WHO IT SUITS
History lovers, families and first-time visitors.

WHO MAY PREFER ANOTHER TOUR
Capitol interior tours can be arranged in advance; ask us.

PRACTICAL INFORMATION
Security screening is required at the Capitol, the Library of Congress and the museums. Summers are hot and humid.

days.name: Arlington, the memorials of the National Mall, the White House, a Smithsonian museum and the Capitol
days.description:
What to expect: the capital's monuments and history, with a local guide and private vehicle.

Your guide and driver collect you at about 8:30 and cross the Potomac to Arlington National Cemetery, where more than 400,000 service members and veterans are buried. You visit the grave of President John F. Kennedy and its eternal flame, and watch the solemn changing of the guard at the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier.

Back in the city, you walk the western end of the Mall: the Lincoln Memorial, with Daniel Chester French's seated statue, where Martin Luther King Jr. gave his 'I Have a Dream' speech in 1963; the black granite wall of the Vietnam Veterans Memorial, designed by Maya Lin; the Korean War Veterans Memorial and the World War II Memorial. You drive past the Jefferson Memorial on the Tidal Basin and see the White House from Lafayette Square.

After lunch (not included), you spend an hour in a Smithsonian museum of your choice, such as the National Air and Space Museum or the National Museum of African American History and Culture. You end at the Capitol, the seat of Congress, and the Library of Congress, whose Great Hall is one of the most splendid interiors in the country.

SCHEDULE (approximate times)
08:30 – Pick-up at your hotel.
09:00 – Arlington National Cemetery.
10:45 – Lincoln Memorial and the war memorials.
12:00 – Jefferson Memorial and the White House.
12:45 – Lunch break.
14:00 – Smithsonian museum.
15:30 – Capitol and Library of Congress.
16:45 – Back at your hotel.

GOOD TO KNOW
• An evening monuments tour, when the memorials are lit, can be arranged.
• The cherry blossoms bloom around the Tidal Basin in late March and early April.

INCLUDED: private vehicle and driver, local guide, bottled water, hotel pick-up and drop-off.
NOT INCLUDED: lunch, tips.

Overnight: none.
Meals: none.

faq.question: How does booking on request work?
faq.answer: You choose a date and the number of travellers and send the request. Nothing is charged. We confirm availability and the final price by email within 24 hours, and you pay online only when the tour is confirmed.

faq.question: Can we go inside the Capitol or the White House?
faq.answer: Capitol tours can be booked in advance; White House tours require a request through your embassy or a member of Congress months ahead.

faq.question: Are the museums free?
faq.answer: Yes, the Smithsonian museums are free; some require timed passes, which we arrange.

faq.question: Is lunch included?
faq.answer: No. Your guide suggests a museum café or a restaurant nearby.

faq.question: Is it suitable for children?
faq.answer: Yes. Children love the Air and Space Museum. Child seats are provided free of charge on request.

faq.question: Is it suitable for people with limited mobility?
faq.answer: Yes. The monuments and museums are accessible, and the vehicle can drop you close.

faq.question: Can we see the cherry blossoms?
faq.answer: Yes, in late March or early April, around the Tidal Basin.

faq.question: Can we add Mount Vernon?
faq.answer: Yes, George Washington’s estate, about 30 minutes away, on a longer day.

faq.question: Will we be taken to shops?
faq.answer: No. There are no commission stops.

faq.question: What should we wear?
faq.answer: Comfortable shoes and light clothes in summer; layers in winter.

faq.question: What is the best time of year?
faq.answer: Spring and autumn. Summer is hot and humid.

faq.question: Should we tip?
faq.answer: Tipping is customary in the United States: 15 to 20 percent is usual for guides and drivers if you were happy with the service, but it is always your choice.

faq.question: What is the cancellation policy?
faq.answer: You can cancel free of charge up to 24 hours before the tour. Until your request is confirmed, nothing is charged at all.
